# adjudicate — full brief

> Guardrails for AI agents: a deterministic control layer between LLM tool-calls and execution. Every state-mutating AI action crosses the kernel as an IntentEnvelope and is adjudicated to exactly one of six outcomes, then recorded as a tamper-evident, replay-verifiable audit receipt (with an optional cryptographic signature for non-repudiation).

## What it is

adjudicate is a decision kernel for AI actions. An LLM-driven agent does not call your tools or APIs directly; it *proposes* an action, and the kernel *disposes* — deciding whether that action should run, change, wait, escalate to a human, or stop. The decision is deterministic: given the same `(envelope, state, policy)` the kernel returns a byte-identical outcome, and every decision is written to an append-only audit ledger.

The kernel `@adjudicate/core` is at v1.x — published to npm & API-stable (additive-only; no breaking changes within v1). Packs and primitives are evolving at v0.2–0.3.

## The problem it solves

LLM agents that hold real tool-calls turn a prompt-injection, a hallucination, or a runaway loop into a real side-effect: a destructive command, a data exfiltration, a runaway API bill, an unapproved production deploy. Binary allow/deny is too blunt — it either blocks useful work or lets risky work through. adjudicate inserts a typed, auditable control layer with six graded outcomes instead of two, so a risky action can be rewritten, deferred, or routed to a human rather than only allowed or refused.

## The six decision outcomes

- EXECUTE — the intent runs against the side-effect.
- REFUSE — the intent is rejected with a structured refusal (a basis code, never a silent drop).
- REWRITE — the kernel returns a sanitised replacement intent (e.g. PII masked, blast radius clamped, an unsafe flag removed).
- DEFER — the intent is parked until an external signal arrives (a dependency recovers, a review resolves).
- ESCALATE — the intent is routed to a human approver; the parked request is resumable.
- REQUEST_CONFIRMATION — the kernel asks for an affirmative re-confirmation before proceeding.

## The IntentEnvelope (v2)

Every action crosses the kernel as an IntentEnvelope — the canonical mutation proposal. It has nine top-level fields, plus an optional `resourceRefs`:

- `version` — envelope schema version (currently 2).
- `kind` — the intent type string (e.g. `deployment.approval.request`, `terminal.run`, `support.ticket.create`).
- `payload` — the action's arguments.
- `createdAt` — ISO-8601 wall-clock timestamp; descriptive metadata, NOT part of the hash.
- `nonce` — adopter-supplied idempotency key; part of the hash. Retries of the same logical action reuse the same nonce so the ledger can dedupe.
- `actor` — `{ principal: "llm" | "user" | "system", sessionId: string }` (optional reserved `attestation`).
- `taint` — `SYSTEM | TRUSTED | UNTRUSTED` provenance label.
- `origin` — declared provenance origin of the intent; always present and bound into the hash, so a declared origin cannot be flipped after the fact.
- `resourceRefs` — optional references to the resources the intent touches; part of the hash when present.
- `intentHash` — `sha256` over the canonical JSON of `(version, kind, payload, nonce, actor, taint, origin, and resourceRefs when present)`. Verified by the kernel, not trusted; a forged/drifted hash is refused with `schema:intent_hash_mismatch`.

## The audit receipt

Each decision yields an AuditRecord binding the envelope, the decision, and the basis. Tamper-evidence is two cryptographic fields:

- `auditHash` — `sha256Canonical(record \ { auditHash, signature, metadata })`. Binds envelope + decision + basis + supersession into one content hash; re-derivable for tamper detection.
- `signature` — an optional, pluggable cryptographic signature over `auditHash`, adding non-repudiation. (auditHash alone gives tamper detection; the signature adds attribution.)

Because the decision is deterministic and content-addressed, the whole ledger is replay-verifiable: re-running the recorded envelopes reproduces the recorded hashes.

## Install (real npm packages)

- `pnpm add @adjudicate/core` — the published, API-stable v1 kernel (additive-only).
- Adapters: `@adjudicate/anthropic`, `@adjudicate/openai`.
- CLI: `@adjudicate/cli`.
- Governance packs (`@adjudicate/pack-*`):
  - `@adjudicate/pack-incident-response` — incident → remediation lifecycle exercising all six outcomes.
  - `@adjudicate/pack-access-governance` — least-privilege clamps, sensitive-resource escalation, confirmed revokes.
  - `@adjudicate/pack-deployments-approval` — release-gating: ramp clamp, approval/eval-score escalation, zone-bounded green-region clamp.

## Capabilities (selected)

- PII / data-classification guard — masks classified data (SSNs, cards, secrets) via REWRITE, taint preserved.
- Command-risk guard — classifies a terminal command and chooses EXECUTE / REWRITE / REQUEST_CONFIRMATION / REFUSE; never echoes the raw command.
- Token-budget guard — enforces a per-session token budget held in audited state; REFUSE/DEFER once the cap is crossed.
- Red Team — deterministic adversarial test suite reporting how many attack vectors the kernel refused.
- Behavioral drift — detects statistical drift in the decision-outcome distribution over time.
- AI bill-of-materials — signable manifest of every model, pack, guard and adapter in the deployment.
- Configuration integrity seal — verifiable hash of the active policy/pack config so tampering is detectable.
- Smart approval engine — registry + channels turning ESCALATE into a resumable human-in-the-loop step.
